messages:
cheng: quick thread — I ran a small eval last night on long multi-turn sessions and saw weird KV fragmentation + steady memory climb even when hit-rate looked stable. attaching notes below.

alyssa: ack, curious what you mean by "fragmentation" here. is it many tiny allocations or a lot of partially-used blocks?

cheng: both. short summary: sessions that interleave many distinct prefixes generate many small KV entries (~1–4k each). over ~2000 requests/session we end up with ~120k small chunks instead of a few larger coalesced segments.

kyle: ugh that sounds like allocator churn + page waste. any heap profiles?

cheng: yes — ran heap/profile and runtime KV pages show ~78% utilization in terms of live keys but only ~42% memory compaction due to fragment boundaries. captured flame graph and a quick metric sample: `session_id=svc-A`, requests=2.1k, unique_prefixes=9.1k, kv_entries=121,340, kv_memory=1.9GB, useful_kv_bytes=820MB.

tara: that's a big gap. did you try prefix concat heuristics? earlier ideas were to concat contiguous prefixes in the same session when keys are small.

cheng: exactly. I prototyped a small concat pass that runs on append: if new prefix key is < 8KB and the previous tail key in the session is < 8KB and both are same model+seq range, we concat them into a single backing segment and remap key offsets. results: kv_entries down 58%, memory down 32%, latency overhead +0.6ms per append.

ashok: how did you handle eviction/ttl? if we concat, evicting a single logical prefix shouldn't force throwing away unrelated data.

cheng: we maintained sub-key offsets and a lightweight index so we can drop subranges. eviction algorithm changed from plain LRU per-key to segmented LRU with per-segment subranges. I sketched config: 

```
kv.eviction.strategy = "segmented_lru"
kv.segment.max_size = 64KB
kv.subrange.granularity = 1KB
kv.compact.threshold = 0.25  # fraction of wasted bytes to trigger compaction
```

kyle: that config looks reasonable. seg-LRU + compaction should reduce fragmentation but adds CPU for compaction. numbers?

cheng: compaction cost: background task compacts 120MB/min on worst session, CPU increase ~6% on p3.2xLarge probe. Most compaction happens during quiescent spikes so tail latency impact minimal.

tara: any effect on cache reuse across requests? the original problem was prefix reuse across different requests where first token sequences match a prior session.

cheng: positive. after concat and segmented indexing, cross-request reuse improved 12% because common short prefixes no longer spread across many tiny entries and get looked up as a contiguous match. hit-latency improved ~4–6ms p50.

perf-bot: nightly-kv-eval: run=kv-compact-proto-3, delta_memory=-32%, delta_entries=-58%, delta_cross_session_hit_rate=+12%.

ashok: sounds promising. downside: complexity + more metadata per segment. how much index overhead?

cheng: index overhead ~5% extra memory (per-segment offsets + refcounts). tradeoff seems fine. edge cases: if a session frequently mutates earlier prefixes (patching), we pay compaction/merge cost. need heuristics to detect churn and skip concat for hot-mutable prefixes.

alyssa: can we instead do opportunistic backfill coalescing on read? i.e., when we see many adjacent small keys read in sequence, merge them then instead of on write. reduces cost for highly mutable writes.

cheng: good idea — I tried read-triggered compact: reduced unnecessary concat by ~40% and still got 45% reduction in entries. implementation note: need to acquire short-lived locks to atomically replace segments.

kyle: be careful about concurrency on hot prefixes. even short locks can add up. consider RCU-style pointer swaps for segment replacement.

cheng: noted. next steps I propose:
- ship concat prototype behind feature flag (session-concat=true) on staging
- toggle read-triggered mode as default and measure tail latency for 48h
- add a compaction metric + alert if compaction CPU > 12% baseline or background IO grows
- add unit tests for subrange eviction correctness and A/B traffic to capture regressions

tara: +1. also create a perf regression job that runs long-session traces (2k+ reqs) every deploy.

ashok: can you paste the small comparator app or a quick pseudo patch so infra can gate?

cheng: pasted minimal pseudo below: 
```
// on append
if (new_key.size < 8KB && tail.size < 8KB && tail.model==new_key.model) {
  segment = tail.segment
  segment.append(new_key.data)
  index.add_subrange(segment.id, offset, len)
} else {
  allocate_new_segment(new_key)
}
```

alyssa: cool. if you want I can own the staging rollout and define the A/B metrics.

cheng: awesome — tagging you on the PR when ready. thanks all, filing follow-ups: GH issue #1453 (concat-evict-proto), and I'll push the profiling traces to S3 `s3://redwood-perf/kv/concat/2065432100/`

kyle: thanks — this feels like a solid middle ground vs heavy-handed gc. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: alert-suppression: enabled for kv-compact-proto-3 until 2065433000

tara: cool — keep notes of any regressions, especially on small models where prefixes are more numerous.

cheng: will do. closing thread for now, will update when PR is up.
